name: maybe_Actor_LinkSubObjectNodes
summary: Resolves sub-object handles through Field_GetObjectHandleA/B and stores the matching node pointers into the actor's render-node fields at +0x8B and +0x98. The 4.9 KB body is a mis-split block: most of it cannot be the same function, so only the handle-getter flow and the two final stores are trusted.
evidence: The one named caller Field_Action_EvaluateTurnDirection and the two named handle getters support a link/resolve step, but the callee list (Snd_DetachChannel, GetSmallMedalNum, Mem_AllocAligned_2 ...) cannot follow from the visible flow and the body still uses unaff_r6..unaff_r11, i.e. a damaged/mis-split decompilation. No new evidence identifies the sub-objects.

name: maybe_Ui_PartList_RemoveAndRebuild

params.id: part id to remove from the widget's +0xA0..+0x118 list

summary: Removes one id from a UI object's fixed 16-bit part-id list (+0xA0..+0x118) and rebuilds the remaining entries: each id is looked up in the part array (+4, stride 0xE), entries whose part is in anim state 1 are re-appended, and the gap is filled with 0xFFFF.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Ui_SkillPanel_HandleInput and the callee is the confident Ui_Part_GetAnimState (0.55), so the remove-and-rebuild-by-anim-state reading is supported; the body is still decompiler-damaged (unaff_r10 plus an in_r12 pseudo-register), so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Ui_MessagePartTable_Ctor
signature: UiMessagePartTable* Ui_MessagePartTable_Ctor(UiMessagePartTable* storage, int kind, u32* out)
summary: In-place constructor of the message part table: initialises the three intrusive list heads, the 0x900-byte part area, the 0xFFFF sentinels and the 0x60-entry index; the non-first path then adds the six glyph parts of the command by id.
evidence: NEW: the class is confirmed by its siblings Ui_MessagePartTable_Dtor (0x3E2A58) and Ui_MessagePartTable_Create (0x3E2914) in the same block, and the only caller is Ui_MessagePage_ExecuteCommand. The damaged tail (halt_baddata, unreachable blocks) affects the second half only; the constructor half is intact.

name: Field_Actor_SetWeaponAnimTime

params.randomize: nonzero adds RNG jitter to the computed start time

summary: Computes the weapon-animation start value at +0x230: (f_228 + f_254 + 1) * 16, or a randomised/scaled variant built from the game RNG at (work+8)+0x98 when randomize is set.
evidence: NEW: the whole Field_Actor weapon-animation block is now named (Field_Actor_ApplyWeaponAnim 0x3E8AEC, Field_Actor_UpdateWeaponAnim 0x3E8F84, Field_Actor_UpdateWeaponAttach 0x3E87B4), and Field_Npc_RefreshModelVariant (0.50) calls this routine during model-variant setup to seed the +0x230 value the apply step consumes. The RNG call func_0051B1FC on the game RNG confirms the jitter, not a UI timer.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DeletingDtor_vt7743A0

params.vtable: most-derived class vtable installed by the caller

summary: Deleting destructor of a Ui widget-derived class: installs the caller's vtable, releases the two pack handles at +0x4F/-4, restores the base Ui_AllocWidget vtable 0x7743A0 on the embedded widget at -0x134, releases its cached model, runs Gfx_SceneNode_DtorBase and frees the block.
evidence: The vtable slot content confirms the family: 0x47E944 Ui_AllocWidget_Dtor and 0x47E984 Ui_AllocWidget_DtorBase install the same base vtable 0x7743A0; this copy is one of three byte-identical deleting dtors (also 0x4A84D4 and 0x4A8A38). Which derived class passes which vtable is still unknown, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DeletingDtorB_vt7743A0

params.vtable: most-derived class vtable installed by the caller

summary: Second byte-identical copy of the Ui widget deleting destructor at 0x42AAF4: same pack-handle release, same restore of the base Ui_AllocWidget vtable 0x7743A0, same scene-node teardown and free.
evidence: CORRECTED: the old 'StatusPanel' label had no support at all (no caller, no vtable evidence); the body is identical to 0x42AAF4, whose family is fixed by Ui_AllocWidget_Dtor/Ui_AllocWidget_DtorBase. The letter suffix keeps the three template copies apart; the owning class is still unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_Widget_DeletingDtorC_vt7743A0

params.vtable: most-derived class vtable installed by the caller

summary: Third byte-identical copy of the Ui widget deleting destructor at 0x42AAF4 (same handle release, base vtable 0x7743A0, scene-node teardown and free).
evidence: CORRECTED: 'StatusPanel' was a first-pass guess with no evidence; the body matches 0x42AAF4/0x4A84D4 exactly apart from the caller-supplied vtable. Only the family (Ui_AllocWidget base vtable 0x7743A0) is proven, not the derived class.

name: maybe_Ui_AllocWidget_DeleteDtor_vt780820
summary: Deleting destructor at slot 0 of vtable 0x780820: runs the Ui_AllocWidget base teardown (0x47E984) and frees the block. The class is not a Monster_ModelInstance.
evidence: CORRECTED: the confident Monster_ModelInstance_Dtor (0x421674) and DtorB (0x422B84) belong to vtables 0x7808B4 and 0x780A20 and do much more (anim refs, pattern model, pack handles); this 16-byte routine only calls Ui_AllocWidget_DtorBase + free, so it is the deleting dtor of whatever class owns vtable 0x780820. The class name is still unknown, hence the vtable-based name.

name: Camera_SetYawNormalized
signature: void Camera_SetYawNormalized(Camera* self, u32 snap, float yaw)

params.snap: nonzero also rebuilds the stored yaw quaternion
params.yaw: incoming angle in degrees, arriving in s0 (Ghidra lost it)

summary: Normalises the incoming angle to [0, 360), writes it to the camera yaw fields +0x118/+0x11C and, when snap is set, rebuilds the yaw quaternion at +0x128..+0x134.
evidence: CORRECTED: there is no spring/filter state in the body at all - it is a 360-degree wrap (divide by 360, floor via func_006731EC, multiply back) plus a quaternion refresh. The caller Camera_SetFocusOffsetAndBlend (0.55) and the IECamera vtable place it in the camera angle path, so the 'spring' wording was wrong.

name: Ui_PointText_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the point-text widget: runs Ui_Object_CtorBase, clears the word at +0x4C and installs vtable 0x77A1A0.
evidence: CORRECTED: vtable 0x77A1A0 is the Ui_PointText class vtable - the sibling Ui_PointText_Init (0x4DB238, 0.50) documents the same vtable and binds 'txt_point_l'/'txt_point_r'. The caller is the confident Ui_SkillPanel_Ctor, which builds the skill panel's point display. The old vtable-only name hid the class.

name: maybe_Svc_Object_Dtor
summary: Base destructor of the service-object protocol: installs the class vtable 0x780EF0, flushes the buffered handle through Svc_Ipc_Send080E0080 when one is pending, then clears the session, buffer and handle words.
evidence: CORRECTED: the block 0x505214..0x505780 is the Svc_Object family (Cmd1..Cmd9, ReleaseRef, CreateBare, Destroy) and this entry is the only one that writes the class vtable itself and then zeroes every member, i.e. the destructor, not a numbered command. The old 'Cmd9' and 'ReleaseAndReset' wordings both mixed a call number with a teardown.

name: Svc_Cecd_OpenRawFile
summary: Opens the raw CECD file: dispatches CECD command 0x03 to whichever of the two session slots is active (Cmd0003 or the B variant) and returns.
evidence: NEW: CECD command numbering (0x03 = Open, 0x07 = Read) plus the confident siblings Svc_Cecd_WriteRawFile (0x50C3CC), Svc_Cecd_DeleteRawFile (0x50C474) and Svc_Cecd_OpenService (0x50C520) put this wrapper in the raw file open/read/write/delete set; its caller is the open-retry wrapper. The two-slot dispatch is only session bookkeeping, not a different operation.

name: Svc_Cecd_ReadRawFile
summary: Reads the raw CECD file: dispatches CECD command 0x07 to the active session slot (Cmd0007 or the B variant).
evidence: NEW: CECD command 0x07 = Read, the wrapper sits in the same raw-file block as Svc_Cecd_OpenRawFile/WriteRawFile/DeleteRawFile, and its caller is Svc_Cecd_ReadWithRetry (0x50BF64). Only the session-slot selection is unresolved detail.

name: Model_PartAnim_UpdateTracks

params.deltaTime: arrives in s0; advances each slot timer

summary: Advances up to three 0x40-byte layered part-animation slots (timer, then linear or sine interpolation of offset/scale/rotation/colour) and writes the results into the target render nodes, stopping a slot when its duration expires.
evidence: NEW: three named callers drive it for model overlays - Gfx_Model_DrawOverlayPasses (0x2D423C), Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_BlendPresets (0x61F618) and Ui_WorldMap_LoadModels - and the same three-slot block is the generic layered-part animator, so the old 'ModelFaceParts'/'face' reading was too narrow. The interpolation and slot-stop logic are visible in the body.

name: maybe_Math_WrapFloatToU16

params.limit: upper bound for the fmodf wrap

summary: Wraps a float into [0, limit) with fmodf, then truncates to an unsigned 16-bit value with the current FPSCR rounding mode and converts the result back to float. The name describes the arithmetic only; the owner (CRT helper vs. sound driver) is unknown.
evidence: No caller can be trusted: the six reported callers (Fs_CheckPendingResult, four Fx_Billboard_* routines and Math_Vector3_DistanceSquared) do not share a float-to-u16 wrap step, which points at a shared CRT/compiler helper in the std_FastSinCos/std_Fmodf block rather than at those call sites. The body still drops the result register, so even the return type is inferred.

name: Gfx_CmdBuf_EmitStateBlob
signature: u32* Gfx_CmdBuf_EmitStateBlob(GfxCmdBuf* self, u32* out, u32* flags)

params.out: write pointer into the GPU command stream

summary: Emits an eight-word GPU state header (PICA command words 0x0002006F / 0x00200080, 0x1000) into the command stream, copies the object's inline descriptor (pointer at +8, size f_C) after it and advances the write pointer; the caller's flags are used to mark the state as set.
evidence: NEW: both callers are the confident Ui_LayoutText_SetupLineState / Ui_LayoutText_RegisterDefaultState, which hand it a text line-state descriptor; the emitted PICA command words and the memcpy of the inline blob are exactly what the name claims. The name deliberately says 'blob' because the descriptor contents are still unidentified.

name: maybe_Battle2DUnit_DtorDeleting

params.vtable: most-derived class vtable installed by the caller

summary: Deleting destructor of the 2D battle-unit container: stores the class vtable, destroys the embedded party display at +0x17E8 (base vtable 0x774568), runs the base destructor and frees the block.
evidence: The neighbouring block is the 2D battle-unit UI (Battle2DUnit_BindPartyMember 0x59F36C just before, Battle_Ui_* methods after), and the vtable 0x774568 members are FieldParty/Battle_Ui methods, so 'Battle2DUnit' is plausible - but the confident Battle2DUnit_Dtor at 0x5A1994 belongs to a different class (vtable 0x77EAC0), so this stays a maybe_ with the container wording kept.

name: maybe_Battle2DUnit_DtorNoFree

params.vtable: most-derived class vtable installed by the caller

summary: Non-deleting destructor paired with 0x59F45C: installs the class vtable, destroys the embedded party display at +0x17E8 and calls the base destructor without freeing the object.
evidence: CORRECTED wording: the plain name Battle2DUnit_Dtor is already taken by the confident function at 0x5A1994 (different class, vtable 0x77EAC0); this entry is the no-free variant of the 0x59F45C pair (it stops after the base ctor/party teardown). The owning class is still not proven.

name: Gfx_SpriteActor_RefreshAndPlayAnim
summary: Refreshes the sprite actor's model/cell visibility, plays the animation id held in the global at 0x00727940 and then calls the actor vtable slot +0x40 with state 4.
evidence: NEW: the callees are named (Field_SceneObject_RefreshModelAndCellVisibility, Anim_PlayByIdForActor) and the confident sibling Gfx_SpriteActor_StopAnimAndHide sits at 0x5C86A0, so the refresh+play sequence and the class are both supported. Only the meaning of state 4 is unknown, and the name does not claim it.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_UpdatePathMotion

params.frame: receives the sampled position and tangent

summary: Advances a gimmick along its path: steps the phase (+0x1C by +0x18), clamps it against the arc-length table at +0xC indexed by +0x14, sets the finished byte +0x20 at the end, then writes the sampled position/tangent into the caller's frame record.
evidence: NEW: both path readers are now confident (Field_Path_GetPosition 0x714008, Field_Path_GetTangent 0x713DB0) and Math_MatrixInverse is called for the frame, so the path-sampling reading holds; but there is no caller and the sample-write half is still decompiler-damaged, so it stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Gfx_SpritePane_FindMaterialValueByName

params.manager: object owning the name-lookup vtable slot +0x2C
params.name: pane/layout object name (the caller passes pointers to 'poker_card_*' strings)

summary: Looks up a layout object by name through the manager's vtable slot +0x2C, checks the result against the sprite-pane vtable 0x007AE8A4 and returns its primary material's +0x78 word (0 when absent).
evidence: CORRECTED: the caller Ui_PokerWindow_ResolveCardObjects (0.60) passes a pointer to a name string as the second argument, so the 'componentId' reading was wrong; the callee is Gfx_SpritePane_GetPrimaryMaterial and the returned word is stored in the card-handle slots. What +0x78 exactly is (texture vs. material handle) is still open, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Gfx_SetGlobalPair
summary: Publishes two words into the global pair at 0x007AE5B4 and re-initialises the critical section at 0x007CF360 with flags 0x04000048.
evidence: CORRECTED subsystem: the caller is Gfx_InitVramBanks and the immediate neighbours are Gfx_ResetGlobalPair (0x6B9060), Gfx_Vram_SetAllocatorWithDefaults (0x6B90A8) and the Gfx_Movie_* block, so neither 'Sq_' nor 'Os_' was right; the pair's contents (probably VRAM allocator state) are still unidentified, hence 0.4.

name: Path_BuildArcLengthTable
signature: void Path_BuildArcLengthTable(void* self, u32 count, int nodeSize, int alignment, int poolId)

params.poolId: nonzero also fills the alternate table at +4

summary: Builds the path's cumulative arc-length table: allocates nodeSize*0x30 bytes, evaluates the cubic curve between consecutive points (basis weights 0.125/0.25/0.5), accumulates the segment lengths and marks the path as built.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Path_BuildFromPoints (0x4B63D8), which calls this right after Path_ComputeDirections; the allocation shape, the cubic weights and the cumulative sum are visible in the body, so the 'Mem_AllocAlignedNodeChain' reading only described the first allocation.

name: maybe_std_GetTerminateState
summary: Lazily creates the CRT terminate-state record: allocates 0x20 bytes, stores the default terminate handler 0x001000FD at +8, clears the remaining fields and attaches the 0x88-byte scratch block from 0x001000BA; returns the cached record.
evidence: The callee is the confident Mem_Alloc (0.75) and the caller is std_RunTerminateHandler, so the record/handler shape is clear; but that caller is itself only 0.45, and the scratch-block helper at 0x001000B8 is unnamed, so the 'terminate' semantics are not independently confirmed.

name: Snd_OpenService
summary: Opens the sound service session (result stored in the 0x007F2358 service block at +0xC) and starts the worker thread with Os_CreateThreadWithStack (entry 0x0010BDF4, 0x228-byte stack); a negative handle is reported through 0x00118100.
evidence: NEW: the whole 0x107544..0x1076AC block is the Snd family (Snd_Initialize, Snd_Shutdown, Snd_UpdateState, Snd_IsRunning), and both callees are named (Svc_SendRequestIpc, Os_CreateThreadWithStack). Open-session + start-worker is exactly the body; the only uncertainty is which nn service name the request carries.

name: maybe_Snd_CommandRing_Reserve
signature: u32* maybe_Snd_CommandRing_Reserve(u32* ring, int count, u32* out)
summary: Reserves count contiguous free words in the sound command ring used by Snd_QueueCommandBuffer, tracking the ring read/write positions across the wrap and returning a pointer to the free run (or 0).
evidence: The ring helper it calls is the same Os_QueueTryPop (0x0011B57C) block as the sound/stream command ring, which supports the subsystem; but Ghidra gave up on most of the body (unaff_r4, coprocessor_function, halt_baddata), so the reserve arithmetic cannot be verified and the name stays a low-confidence maybe_.

name: maybe_Hid_UpdateCalibration
summary: When the calibration slot at 0x007AF0DC is active, reads the current calibration id with IPC command 0x13 and, if the reply is 0xC9405001, acknowledges it with command 0x3D.
evidence: NEW: the two command wrappers are now named by their headers (Os_IpcSendCommand13 reads a byte, Os_IpcSendCommand3D sends one), so the read-compare-acknowledge shape is confirmed; that the ids are HID calibration data is still an inference from the HID-side reading, and the caller Gfx_IpcCmd4F0080 does not fit that story, so maybe_ stays.

name: Ui_Cue_Start
signature: int Ui_Cue_Start(UiCue* cue, u16 cueId, u32 param1, u32 param2, u32 param3, int startMode)

params.startMode: 0 runs the start callback, nonzero the stop callback

summary: Starts a UI cue on an idle cue object: stores the cue id, the three packed parameters and the start/stop flag, invokes the matching sound-player callback, copies the initial callback pair and returns 1 (0 when the cue was busy).
evidence: NEW: the five neighbours Ui_Cue_Finish (0x284AE4), Ui_Cue_Update, Ui_Cue_ResetIfIdle, Ui_Cue_StopBgm and this entry form one Ui_Cue class in the 0x284A..0x284C block; the idle test, cue-id write and Sound_GetPlayer callback selection (0x001EE220 / 0x001EE018) are visible. The three packed parameters are passed in s1..s3 and are still unnamed.

name: maybe_Field_IsEventMode
summary: Field-mode flag test: returns 1 only when bit 0x80 of the per-world byte at work+0x2A474 is SET and the map-mode value read from work+0x24A98 (helper 0x0066B17C, id 0x15) is <= 0x0E; otherwise 0.
evidence: Corrected an earlier note: 1 requires the bit to be SET (the previous 'inverted polarity' claim came from a misread branch). The neighbours are the field script natives at 0x14FB34..0x150368 (GetScenarioFlag, IsInFollowParty, GimmickDoorOpen...), so it is a script-callable field predicate; what bit 0x80 and modes 0..0x0E mean is still undecoded.

name: maybe_Ui_PlayWindowSeByState

params.win: window instance; only played when it is an instance of the class at 0x007C4E50

summary: Plays the window transition sound for one window instance: after the class-chain check it plays SE table index 0x16 or 0x17, chosen by the byte at win+0x342. Nothing is closed or destroyed here.
evidence: CORRECTED: the disassembly shows moveq r2,#0x16 / movne r2,#0x17 feeding the named Sound_PlaySeFromTable (the decompiler showed the dropped register args as a second argument 0), and the state byte is at win+0x342. The old 'CloseWindowOfType' described a close that never happens; whether 0x16/0x17 mean open/close of the transition is still unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_PlayWindowSeByState2

params.win: window instance; only played when it is an instance of the class at 0x007C4E50

summary: Second variant of the window transition sound helper: plays SE table index 0x18 or 4, chosen by the byte at win+0x35C, after the class-chain check.
evidence: CORRECTED: the disassembly shows moveq r2,#0x18 / movne r2,#4 with the same Sound_PlaySeFromTable call and the class literal 0x007C4E50 as 0x15B118; the only difference is the state byte offset (+0x35C instead of +0x342). So this is a second instance of the same SE helper, not a close routine.

name: Battle_QueueCommand0x15
signature: void Battle_QueueCommand0x15(void* queue, u32* action, u32* out)

params.action: action/unit record whose flags are derived

summary: Pushes battle command 0x15: computes the turn-order priority with Battle_CalcTurnOrderPriority, derives two flag words from the action (byte table at 0x00169DBC, mode byte f_10, byte +0xB108) and appends the entry through Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry with mode 7.
evidence: NEW: both callees are now confident (Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry 0.60, Battle_CalcTurnOrderPriority) and the literal 0x15 is the command id handed to the push; the siblings pushing 0x00 and 0x16 keep the three comparable. The meaning of command 0x15 itself is unknown, which is why the name is id-based.

name: Battle_QueueCommand0x00

params.action: unit/action whose vtable +0xE8 state is tested

summary: Pushes battle command 0: when the unit's vtable +0xE8 reports state 0x7D the same entry is pushed twice (the following action lands one slot later), otherwise once; the turn-order priority is computed identically for both.
evidence: NEW: the callees are the confident Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry and Battle_CalcTurnOrderPriority, the pushed id is the literal 0 and the 0x7D state test is visible; command 0 being an idle/no-op command is still an inference, so the name stays id-based.

name: Battle_QueueCommand0x16
signature: void Battle_QueueCommand0x16(void* queue, u32* action, u32* out)

params.action: action/unit record whose flags are derived

summary: Pushes battle command 0x16: same body as 0x00169D1C but with the byte table at 0x00175C18, deriving two flag words and appending through Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry with mode 7.
evidence: NEW: the callee chain is named (Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry, Battle_CalcTurnOrderPriority) and the id literal 0x16 is passed to the push; body is byte-identical to the 0x15 sibling apart from the id and table base, so the three id-named functions are consistent.

name: maybe_Field_InitNpcAction

params.speed: arrives in s0 (lost by Ghidra) and is cached at +0x2C

summary: Caches the speed at +0x2C, plays the NPC's action animation pair (packed literals 0x74736F4C / 0x0074754E) on the actor at +0x28 and sets its grid state to 2.
evidence: NEW: both callees are named (Field_NpcPlayActionAnim, Map_PlaceObject), which supports 'NPC action setup'; but there is no caller and the float speed argument is dropped, so whether this is a constructor, a setter or a re-init cannot be decided - the name keeps maybe_.

name: maybe_Actor_SetStateFinished
summary: Completion step of an NPC actor action: detaches the placed map object when f_C5 is set, switches the actor state machine to mode 4, selects the finish animation through vtable +0x84 (constant 0x00332918 when there is no target-bone transform) and clears the pending action id at model+0x2A8.
evidence: NEW: the function sits in the NPC action-handler block (Field_NpcAction_MoveToCoordUpdate before, Field_NpcFallAction_LandedUpdate after) and its callees Battle_Unit_SelectMimicEndCommand / Map_PlaceObject are named, supporting a 'finish this action' step; the handler-table slot and the animation id are not named, so the generic state-finished wording stays and the confidence with it.

name: maybe_Ui_Anim_SetPose

params.poseId: 0x11 -> place as 3, 0x12 -> place as 4, 0x13 -> refresh only

summary: Refreshes the cached level-grid revision for self->f_28 and re-places the preview actor with id 3 (poseId 0x11) or 4 (0x12); 0x13 only refreshes. No animation record is touched, so the 'Anim' part of the name is a guess about the owning class.
evidence: NEW: the callees are the same grid-refresh (maybe_Map_RefreshLevelGrid, 0x179084) and Map_PlaceObject pair used by 0x332DCC, and Container_FindObjectByTypeId is called through func_00619BAC; the body contains no animation-set call, so 'SetPose' is only the short description of the 0x11/0x12/0x13 dispatch.

name: maybe_Actor_OnStateChanged

params.state: 0x13 refreshes the grid only, 0x11 also re-places the object as 3

summary: Actor state hook: for state 0x13 it refreshes the actor's cached level-grid revision; for state 0x11 it does the same and re-places the map object with id 3; other states are ignored.
evidence: NEW: it sits next to Field_NpcAction_Stop and Actor_StopStateAnim and uses the same named Map_PlaceObject/maybe_Map_RefreshLevelGrid pair as 0x0028B084, so 'state change hook' holds; the state ids are still undecoded and there is no caller, hence maybe_.

name: Field_NpcAction_SetupVtable
summary: Builds the NPC action object through Gfx_ObjectDesc_Ctor4, installs its class vtable 0x00758598 and clears the parameter word at +0x2C.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Field_SetupNpcActionScript (0x177864) and the callee is Gfx_ObjectDesc_Ctor4; the body is exactly the two stores the name describes, and there is no other behaviour hidden in it. 'SetupVtable' is kept because the object is created by the callee, not here.

name: maybe_Gfx_Effect2D_CreateStartSlotVariant
summary: Creates one 2D-effect slot from the fixed 'Start' descriptor with handle kind 0xB3 on the 2D-effect manager ((work+8)+0x64) and stores the handle at self+4; the count byte comes from Gfx_GetEntryByteProperty(0,10,2)+1.
evidence: CORRECTED: the descriptor layout is the same as the confident Gfx_Effect2D_CreateSlot (0x3DB7C4), Mem_AllocHandle's manager block is the known work+0x64 2D-effect manager, and the name literal is 'Start' - but the count comes from a data-entry property, not an RNG, so 'RandomCount' was wrong. The kind 0xB3 and the variant meaning are still open.

name: maybe_Ui_CursorWindowPair_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the two-slot cursor host window: Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs vtable 0x77A32C, then default-constructs two 0x50-byte Ui_CursorWindow slots with 0x4DC528. Used by Ui_RouletteWindow_Ctor.
evidence: CORRECTED: Ui_CursorWindow_Dtor (0x4DC540, 0.50) is slot 1 of vtable 0x780B54 and 0x4DC528 installs exactly that vtable, so the two 0x50-byte members are the Ui_CursorWindow objects - this outer object only hosts them. The old name claimed the outer class itself was the cursor window. The host class name is still unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_AnimRefWindow_Ctor

params.value: stored in the trailing field after the eight anim-ref lists

summary: In-place constructor of a window-like object: base ctor, vtable from the literal pool, then eight chained 0x50-byte Ui_AnimRefList members (+0x4C..+0x2CC), a trailing value and a -1 sentinel.
evidence: CORRECTED: the callees are Ui_Object_CtorBase and Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor (both confident) and the body is a constructor with eight anim-ref lists; 'DungeonPlaceWindow' was borrowed from the neighbouring Ui_DungeonPlaceWindow_Create (0x1CF8C0), which operates on a different layout (self+0x13C) and is not a constructor of this object. No caller, so the class stays unnamed.

name: Ui_Window_InitHeader
summary: Constructs a window header: Ui_Object_CtorBase, installs the type tag at +0 and the vtable at +0x4C, self-links the three intrusive list sentinels at +0x54..+0x5C, sets f_19 = 0xFF and byte +0x65 = 4, then copies the default three-word colour/parameter block twice.
evidence: NEW: the very next function is the confident Ui_Window_ReleaseHeader (0x1D0980), so Init/Release are a matched pair; the body was checked instruction by instruction (the lost-argument call is Ui_Object_CtorBase), and the initialisation order matches the header layout the release routine tears down.

name: maybe_Casino_Poker_MatchCardFlags
signature: u32 maybe_Casino_Poker_MatchCardFlags(u32* cards, u32 hand, u32 b)
summary: Card-flag scan used by the poker hand evaluator: compares a card index against two expected values and writes the five per-card 1/0 flags, returning 1/2/0 (or 0xFF when an inner compare fails).
evidence: The recovered entry has size 0 and its leading Ui_Object_CtorBase call is a misdecoded prologue; the body duplicates the tail of the confident Casino_Poker_EvaluateHand (0x416D10, 0.60), which now supports the poker context, but the function boundary itself is suspect and several registers (unaff_r4/r5/r7/r8/r10/r11) are lost, so it stays a low-confidence maybe_.
